newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish market rates may need to rise further - NBP.
newsitem.headline: Polish market rates may need to rise further - NBP.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland may need to further increase market rates in order to control its operational target of reserve money growth after it upped two drainage rates on Tuesday, a senior central bank official said.
The head of the central bank's monetary policy department Jerzy Stopyra said market rates increased because the central bank had to absorb more funds in order to curb reserve money.
"This could mean that controlling the operational target could force us to accept (even) higher rates," Stopyra told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
Asked if the NBP would raise official interest rates, now at 25 percent for the lombard and 22 for the discount, he said:
"If market rates increased to lombard or discount levels we would also have to consider this, but right now we are further tightening our policy on market rates."
On Tuesday the central bank increased the money market's benchmark 14-day reverse repo maximum rate to 22.59 percent from the previous 22.15 percent.
It also increased the maximum yield on its 91-day bills to 22.50 percent from 22.30 percent.
Stopyra said curbing booming domestic demand remained the NBP's top priority and that forecasts were not optimistic.

"According to our forecasts on demand for money in the next few months to a year, credit expansion and possibly (the planned 1998) budget deficit signal that domestic demand will be high, which is our main worry," Stopyra said.

The central bank has called for the government to sharply cut the budget deficit from the planned 2.8 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) this year to 1.5 percent in 1998 and for Poland to balance its books by 1999.

Poland's left-wing coalition government, facing a tough election campaign against right-wing opposition in this September's parliamentary polls, said it wanted to reduce next year's budget deficit to 1.9 percent of GDP.
